editions.text:
The day logged 20 species, 18 by ear and 10 by sight, with 8 seen and heard, across 209 feeder visits. That was quieter than the past-week average of 247.9 visits, while the 657 detections were well above the average of 362.0. Brown-headed Cowbird made up 281 of those detections, all logged between 10:00 and 16:00.

Twelve species were recorded on all seven days, this one included, among them Tufted Titmouse with 80 visits and Carolina Chickadee with 38. Ten species from the past week were not recorded today, including Downy Woodpecker, American Goldfinch, and Pileated Woodpecker. The first visual record of the day was a Northern Cardinal 19 minutes before sunrise, and the last was a Tufted Titmouse 307 minutes after sunrise.

The audio source was switched many times between 07:09 and 08:06 this morning, so the early detections came from changing sources. Brown-headed Cowbird is listed as heard for the first time at this station today, and it was picked up on the audio source in use after those changes, so it is not counted as a new arrival. No species had a first confident visual record at the station today.
